projectBackground.name: Hospital HVAC Retrofit — Level 3 Services
projectBackground.context: Services above the ceiling are congested. Testing and commissioning must finish before the ward reopens.

manager.name: Dieter Hartmann
manager.note: Coordinate before you install. Testing isn't a formality, it's the evidence.

assignment.title: Coordinate, test and commission the services
assignment.brief: Calculate velocities and test pressure, check ducts in Excel, resolve a clash and describe commissioning order.

tasks.title: Pipe Velocity
tasks.prompt: Flow 20 L/s (0.02 m³/s) in a 0.1 m internal diameter pipe. What is the velocity (m/s)?
tasks.mistake: Using radius in the area formula quarters the area.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Test Pressure
tasks.prompt: Test pressure is 1.5 x working pressure. Working pressure is 8 bar. What is test pressure (bar)?
tasks.reasoning: Test above working pressure to prove integrity.
tasks.mistake: Testing at working pressure doesn't prove margin.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Commissioning Order
tasks.prompt: Which order is correct for a water system?
options: Flush and clean, then pressure test, then balance and commission
tasks.reasoning: Debris must be removed before testing and balancing.
tasks.mistake: Skipping flushing damages valves and pumps.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Clash Resolution
tasks.prompt: Select good ways to resolve the duct and pipe clash.
options: Raise an RFI and agree a revised route with the designer
Cut the duct on site and hide it
Check the ceiling height and access after rerouting
Update the coordination model and drawings
tasks.reasoning: Clashes are solved on the model and drawings first.
tasks.tip: Coordinate access as well as space.
tasks.mistake: Site fixes without records cause maintenance problems.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Duct Velocity (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Velocity in column D = B / C (m/s).
tasks.reasoning: D3 has the highest velocity — a noise risk.
tasks.tip: Flag any duct above the limit.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: RFI
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence RFI about the clash.
tasks.modelAnswer: RFI 042: On Level 3 the supply duct (600 x 400) clashes with the chilled water pipe (DN100) above the corridor at grid C-4. Please confirm whether the pipe can be lowered by 150 mm or the duct rerouted, keeping a minimum ceiling height of 2.4 m and maintenance access. Installation of this section is on hold; reply required within three working days to protect the programme.
tasks.reasoning: A good RFI states location, issue, options, constraints and a response date.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Unflushed System
caseStudy.background: A chilled water system was pressure tested but not flushed. Debris blocked control valves and the ward reopened three weeks late.
caseStudy.constraints: Test certificates focused on pressure only.
questions: Why did debris cause a delay?
caseStudy.solution: Hartmann made flush certificates a hold point before testing.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Clean, test, balance, in that order.

quiz.q: The case study was late because:

prompts: Which clash would you resolve first?
What records do you keep during testing?
How do you protect handover dates?
